solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Middle-Easterner said to be in a pub, wet

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the words that follow are judged by how they come out of the mouth

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
wet weather is rainy

explanation.surface: Someone from the Gulf is reported to be sitting in a pub on a wet day.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, BAR RAINY gives the sound of BAHRAINI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bahraini is a native of Bahrain, an island state in the Persian Gulf, so a Middle-Easterner.

clue.text: Rough sound made by donkey on losing tail?

indicators.note: losing its tail means the animal's word drops its last letter

blocks.note: a burro is a small donkey, the Spanish word used in the American southwest

explanation.surface: A donkey that has lost its tail gives a rough noise of complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: BURRO without its final O leaves BURR.
explanation.definitionFit: A burr is a rough rolled pronunciation of R, or a whirring noise, so a rough sound.

clue.text: A time for Pastor in sole US city

indicators.note: one thing for another means the first stands in the place of the second within the word

blocks.note: planta is the anatomical term for the sole of the foot
P is an abbreviation for pastor
taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A clergyman is told it's time to move to a solitary post somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like 'only', but it is the sole of the foot, PLANTA; swap its P for A T to get ATLANTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the state capital of Georgia, a major city in the United States.

clue.text: Injured right away getting round pit lined with stones

indicators.note: away means sent off, so the letter for right is dropped from the preceding word

blocks.note: injured means hurt
R is the abbreviation for right
a round is a circle

explanation.surface: An injured man is carried off and goes around a stone-lined pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' looks like an adjective for the pit; it is the word that loses the letter for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A hut circle is the archaeologist's term for the stone ring left where a prehistoric dwelling stood, often a sunken pit.

clue.text: Fruit and nuts not started

indicators.note: a word that has not started is missing its opening letter

blocks.note: nuts and bananas both mean crazy

explanation.surface: A shopping list of fruit and nuts that nobody has begun on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like food beside 'Fruit', but it means crazy: BANANAS, beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is the pineapple, the name still used in French and other languages and listed in Chambers.

clue.text: Bury more acceptable for a heat exchanger

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
cool means acceptable or fine, so more so is cooler

explanation.surface: Burial is preferred to some engineering device, oddly enough.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercooler is a device that cools air between stages of a compressor or turbocharger, exchanging heat.

clue.text: Warriors involved in counter-claim pilloried

indicators.note: involved in says the word sits inside the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: surface padding: it only makes the phrase a legal counter-claim
found spanning the end of claim and the start of pilloried

explanation.surface: Fighters drawn into a legal counter-claim are publicly ridiculed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across claIM PIlloried; 'counter-' is only surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment or band of armed men, so a body of warriors.

clue.text: Since no longer used, import not concluded

indicators.note: a word not concluded stops short of its final letter

blocks.note: the import of a statement is its meaning or sense

explanation.surface: An unfinished import that has fallen out of use for some time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer used' is part of the definition, flagging an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sens is an obsolete form of since, as Chambers records, hence the archaism marker in the definition.

clue.text: Old battle-axe in dispute beginning to trouble husband

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: to spar is to argue or dispute
first letter of trouble
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A quarrelsome old woman starts making trouble for her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle-axe' tempts as a nagging wife, given 'husband'; here it is the literal weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparth is an archaic word for a battle-axe or halberd, the weapon itself.

clue.text: Boy reportedly discarded sharp instrument

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so its sound counts

blocks.note: Neil is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad is said to have thrown away a sharp tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discarded' marks the word as obsolete, belonging to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Neele is an old spelling of needle, a pointed instrument no longer in use as a word.

clue.text: Dot in Perth has ring about right

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word encloses the letter for right

blocks.note: has can be shortened to 's, as in he's got
to give someone a tinkle is to ring them
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone called Dot in the Scottish city of Perth owns a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot' looks like a woman's name; it is the verb, to dot or sprinkle, in Scots (Perth is in Scotland).
explanation.definitionFit: Strinkle is a Scots word for sprinkle, and to dot something is to sprinkle it lightly.

clue.text: No Parking in rise is a policy reversal

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter for parking is removed

blocks.note: an upturn is a rise
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A council scraps its parking rise in an abrupt change of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the P from UPTURN to leave U-TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-turn is used figuratively for a complete reversal of a government's policy.

clue.text: Pen myth about sexy girl

indicators.note: about means turned around and around, so the letters come out in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer composes a legend about a seductive young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymphet is a sexually attractive girl, a term popularised by Nabokov's Lolita.

clue.text: Chicken and duck from France (not North America) getting official cautions

indicators.note: not here means without, so the two letters for that continent are taken out

blocks.note: chicken and yellow both mean cowardly
canard is French for duck, taken in the plural
NA is the abbreviation for North America

explanation.surface: A French farmyard of poultry is being given formal warnings.
explanation.walkthrough: CANARDS without NA leaves CARDS; 'Chicken and duck' look like poultry, but chicken means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee shows a yellow card as a formal caution to a player who has committed an offence.

clue.text: Row with footballer perhaps left out — he must settle tax bills

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter for left is dropped from the preceding word

blocks.note: to rate someone is to scold them, as is to row them
a footballer is one example of a player
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A footballer is dropped after a row and must still pay his taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: Row rhymes with cow here, meaning tell off. Rates were the UK's local property tax, paid by the ratepayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratepayer is a householder liable for local rates, a property tax, so he pays those bills.

clue.text: Clubs to break old rule for French writer

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it, so the clubs letter goes inside

blocks.note: raine is an old spelling of reign, to rule
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Golf clubs are used to defy an ancient regulation for the sake of a French author.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was a seventeenth-century French dramatist, author of Phèdre.

clue.text: Beetle in brief trip ahead of international sport

blocks.note: a whirl is a short spin or outing
I is the abbreviation for international
gig is an old word for fun or sport

explanation.surface: A beetle goes on a short journey before an international match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' means fun here, as in making sport of someone, and GIG is a Chambers sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The whirligig beetle is a small water beetle that spins rapidly in circles on the surface of ponds.

clue.text: Person at square one not half taken aback by protuberances

indicators.note: not half says only half of that earlier answer is kept, the other half thrown away
aback means backwards, so the letters are read in reverse order

blocks.note: the person is the answer in square one of the grid, the 1-across entry

explanation.surface: Someone back at the starting point is set back by a few bumps.
explanation.walkthrough: Square one is the first square of the grid: 1 Across is BAHRAINI, and its tail AINI reversed gives INIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Inia is the plural of inion, the bony protuberance at the back of the skull.

clue.text: Emperor comes first and sues

blocks.note: Imp. is the abbreviation for Imperator, emperor
whoever comes first leads

explanation.surface: An emperor takes precedence and takes someone to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To implead is a legal term meaning to bring an action against someone, to sue them.

clue.text: Network screens so much of a strip

indicators.note: to screen something is to shield it from view, so one word hides another within it

blocks.note: a LAN is a local area network
the can mean by so much, as in the more the merrier

explanation.surface: A broadcaster vets how much of a comic strip it will show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so much' is the adverb sense of THE, in phrases like 'all the better'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lathen means made of lath, a thin narrow strip of wood, so it is an adjective meaning of a strip.

clue.text: England opener's smashing cricket shot

indicators.note: smashing breaks the words into pieces to be put back together differently

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An England opening batsman plays a superb stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcus Trescothick opened the batting for England's cricket team in the 2000s.
explanation.definitionFit: Trescothick was a regular England opening batsman, so an England opener by name.

clue.text: Century knock grips new Surrey supporter?

indicators.note: to grip is to hold, so one word holds the letter for new inside it

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
a sprig is a small headless nail, something you knock in
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A batsman's hundred holds up the Surrey county cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey looks like the English county with its cricket team; a surrey is a light four-wheeled carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A C-spring is a C-shaped spring that supported the body of a carriage such as a surrey.

clue.text: One's absorbed by soft and hard hats for cricketers

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken in, so it ends up within the other letters

blocks.note: p (piano) is the music abbreviation for soft
an ace is a one in cards
a bowler is a hard felt hat

explanation.surface: Someone is absorbed in a collection of soft and hard hats worn for cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard hats' suggests helmets for batting; they are bowler hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Pace bowlers are fast bowlers in cricket, an example of the cricketers in a side.

clue.text: With love for bit of sketching, ladies coloured images

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter only
with one thing for another tells us to put the first in place of the second
coloured means disguised or distorted, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of sketching
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Women with a love of sketching produce coloured pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the S of LADIES with O to get LADIEO, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Eidola is the plural of eidolon, a phantom or idealised image.

clue.text: Do filling roll for a string player

indicators.note: something filling another sits inside it

blocks.note: a roll is a list of names
do and ut are both names for the first note of the scale

explanation.surface: Instructions to fill a bread roll, for a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb; it is the sol-fa note, older name UT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lutist is someone who plays the lute, a plucked string instrument.

clue.text: Free party in smallest room gets squid

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

blocks.note: the smallest room is a British euphemism for the toilet, the loo
a lig is a free party or freebie event, British slang

explanation.surface: A party with free drinks held in the toilet ends up with a squid.
explanation.walkthrough: A lig is British slang for a free do with food and drink, often a press launch.
explanation.definitionFit: Loligo is the zoological genus of common squid, used in Chambers for the squid itself.

clue.text: In the past guards united at the right time

indicators.note: to guard is to surround and protect, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: once means formerly, in the past
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Historically, guards would work together punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: On cue is an idiom from theatre, meaning exactly when expected, at just the right moment.

clue.text: Not entirely cool person in jug

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the phrase is used, a run of its letters

blocks.note: found across coOL PErson

explanation.surface: Someone not quite cool ends up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' looks like slang for prison, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An olpe is an ancient Greek jug with a pinched spout, a vessel for pouring.

clue.text: Mark gives up independence for another guy

indicators.note: to give something up is to surrender it, so the letter goes

blocks.note: a stain is a mark
I is the abbreviation for independent or independence

explanation.surface: Mark surrenders his freedom on behalf of some other man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' poses as a man's name, matching 'another guy'; it is a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan is a man's name, so another guy alongside the boy Neil of 8 Down.

clue.text: Dress nattier with no end of satin?

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the stated letter is dropped
the end of a word is its final letter only
to dress is also to arrange, so the remaining letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of satin

explanation.surface: Would a dress look smarter without any satin trim?
explanation.walkthrough: NATTIER less N leaves ATTIER, one swap from the answer; 'Dress' does double duty as definition and as the instruction to arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire means clothing in general, and dress is a mass noun for the same thing.

clue.text: County leaving out second-class chaps in forces

indicators.note: leaving out means omitting, so the letter for second-class is dropped

blocks.note: Berks is the abbreviation for Berkshire, an English county
B is the grade below A, so second-class

explanation.surface: A county drops its second-rate men from the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: Erk is British services slang for an aircraftman or naval rating, a low-ranking serviceman.

clue.text: Erratic alto surprisingly outside on pedestals

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected form, so the letters are mixed up
outside means placed around, so the jumbled letters enclose the following one

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for alto
O is a cricket abbreviation for on, the leg side

explanation.surface: An unpredictable alto singer is, surprisingly, put out on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erratic' looks like the anagram signal; it is the fodder, with 'surprisingly' doing the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Acroteria are the plinths at the apex and corners of a pediment that carry statues, so pedestals.

clue.text: Lord's back, fat and stupid

indicators.note: back tells us to read that word from its end

blocks.note: lud is the form of lord in 'm'lud', how barristers address a judge
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A nobleman returns, overweight and dim.
explanation.definitionFit: A dullard is a slow-witted person, and stupid as a noun names the same sort of person.

clue.text: Hard work as before, Harry of Spurs and England's special up front

indicators.note: the letter standing for special moves to the front of the name

blocks.note: Harry Winks played midfield for Tottenham Hotspur and England

explanation.surface: Hard graft is the key to a Spurs and England player's special talent.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club. 'as before' marks the definition as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Swink is an archaic word for toil or hard labour, hence the marker that it was used formerly.

clue.text: Hospital supplies coming from Sweden are defective

indicators.note: defective means faulty, so the letters are out of their proper order

blocks.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Medical supplies imported from Sweden turn out to be faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sera, the plural of serum, are blood fluids used for antitoxins and vaccines that hospitals stock.

clue.text: Head admits good attack upset reserves

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the outer word takes the others inside
upset means overturned, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a ness is a headland, a head
G is the abbreviation for good
to get someone is to attack them, as in get at

explanation.surface: A headteacher confesses that a vicious assault has set back the school's reserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Nest eggs are sums of money saved up for the future, so financial reserves.
